excerpt: Onepin checks and fixes AI voiceover so names, prices and dates are said right, across 30+ voice models including ElevenLabs. Free plan, paid from $16/month, and alternatives.
content:
Onepin is a production layer for AI voiceover. You give it a script and it routes each line to one of more than 30 commercial text-to-speech models (ElevenLabs, OpenAI and Google among them), choosing per line and per language from its own benchmarks. Before synthesis a normaliser rewrites numbers, prices, dates, addresses and abbreviations into how they should be spoken; names and brands are checked against a pronunciation dictionary, which the Product Hunt listing puts at 4 million words. After synthesis every line is scored for word accuracy, naturalness, noise and pronunciation, and failing lines are fixed or regenerated.

Founder Soohyun Bae said on Product Hunt that Onepin's own voice model can fix a mispronounced word without re-rendering the whole take, and that it supports 10 locales with plans for 30. You can work through a chat agent called Quincy that builds a reusable workflow, or through the API, SDK and MCP; Premiere and DaVinci plugins were in development. The team previously built Podonos, a service that scores speech AI.

Onepin launched on Product Hunt on 10 October 2026 and finished #1 for the day, with 384 upvotes and 97 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Onepin ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing, FAQ and About pages and its Product Hunt page, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Web app, API, SDK and MCP
profile.starts_at: Free plan; paid from $16/month billed yearly
profile.summary_short: Routes scripts across 30+ AI voice models and checks and fixes every line, so names, prices and dates are said right

use_cases: Producing product-video voiceovers where brand and product names must be said right
Dubbing and e-learning voiceover in several languages
Checking long audiobook or course scripts line by line without listening to every line
Using your existing ElevenLabs voices with extra validation on top
Fixing internal codenames and acronyms that every voice model gets wrong

paragraphs: Soohyun Bae opened with an example: a great AI voice reads "Porsche Taycan" from the spelling and gets it wrong, and nobody notices because nobody listens to line 1,200. His team spent two years at Podonos measuring how AI voices perform.

He said no AI has ever said his own name correctly, and that wrong names, brands, addresses and medications are a blocker for teams shipping voice at scale. Onepin is the layer that checks and fixes the output instead of regenerating until it sounds right.
launch_story.attribution: Soohyun Bae, founder, on Product Hunt

fit: ship AI voiceover at volume, such as product videos, courses or dubbing
work in several languages and need consistent quality across them
already pay for ElevenLabs or another provider and want validation on top (bring your own key from Studio up)
not_fit: need a Premiere or DaVinci plugin today: the founder said they were in development
need open-source voice models or voice cloning: the FAQ lists both as coming soon
need a language outside its 10 supported ones

pricing.intro: Onepin sells credits through monthly plans; the prices shown are per month when billed yearly (the site says yearly saves 20%). Prices are Onepin's, in US dollars.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 1,000 one-time credits (about 15 minutes of validated audio), auto-routing, mispronunciation fixes, 10 languages, 1 workspace

plans.name: Creator
plans.detail: 3,000 credits a month (about 100 minutes), 3 concurrent runs, 100 GB storage, email support

plans.name: Studio
plans.detail: 15,000 credits a month (about 9 hours), 3 workspaces, bring your own key, Slack support

plans.name: Scale
plans.detail: 50,000 credits a month (about 30 hours), 10 concurrent runs, lowest overage rate

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Output ownership, commercial use on every model, IP indemnity, SSO, SLA

notes: Overage is $0.010 a credit on Creator, $0.008 on Studio and $0.007 on Scale.
Seats are unlimited on every plan.

pros: Fixes a single wrong word without re-rendering the whole take, according to the founder
Works across 30+ voice models, including ones you already pay for
Every line scored for accuracy, naturalness, noise and pronunciation
Free plan without a card and unlimited seats
cons: No open-source models or voice cloning yet

liked: Fixing names and prices that voice models mispronounce
Correcting one word without redoing the recording
asked: Whether a fixed word sounds natural next to the original voice (the founder says it clones the voice and style)
Whether it works with ElevenLabs voices (yes, with your API key)
Whether it plugs into Premiere or DaVinci (in development)
How it handles acronyms and internal codenames

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as Onepin alternatives. Several are voice models Onepin can route to rather than direct rivals. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: ElevenLabs
items.difference: A voice model and studio; Onepin sits on top of it and other models to check and fix output.

items.name: Cartesia Sonic
items.difference: A single low-latency voice model rather than a validation layer across models.

items.name: Fish Audio
items.difference: Offers voice cloning, which Onepin lists as coming soon.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Deepgram and Vapi.

x.none: We found no posts about Onepin on X to link yet.

faq.a: An AI voice production agent: it routes each line of a script to the best of 30+ voice models, cleans up numbers and names first, scores every line, and fixes what fails.
Free with 1,000 one-time credits. Creator is $16 a month, Studio $80 and Scale $240, each billed yearly. Enterprise is custom.

faq.q: Can I use my ElevenLabs account with Onepin?
faq.a: Yes. Bring-your-own-key is available on Studio and above, and the founder said you can use your cloned ElevenLabs voices in Onepin.

faq.q: Does fixing one word mean re-rendering the whole line?
faq.a: No, according to the founder: Onepin's own model fixes the word instead of regenerating the take.
Ten languages today, with more planned, according to its FAQ.
